title: Jack Delaney's father and Delaney's trombone career
summary: Delaney's father drives a cab and played a little alto sax; Jack plays trombone and is returning to Dixieland.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: One question I was going to ask, maybe doesn't belong on here, but Jack Delaney's father, of course, is a taxi driver. Every once in a while, I get in his cab, and was he ever a musician? Would he be a good one? Yes, he did.
Would he be a good one for an interview, you think, for him?
Well, I don't know if he's... Let me...
Okay, we were talking about Jack Delaney's father.

Well, Jack's father just drives a cab just two or three hours a day, mostly to get out the house. He's a retired fireman on pension today. He played a little alto sax in the days where he used to play for the house parties. You know, when he had the little alto sax and C melody, and he never really got to play any jazz or anything like that. Of course, he's got a fine boy there that plays a lot of trombone, Jack. Jack's terrific. He has the makings. I think Jack will be in years to come if he sticks to the Dixieland.
Well, he's working at the hotel there the last few years.

He's up to with that now. Yeah, he took it away from him a little, but he's getting back into the Dixieland vein now, and he'll probably come back. He's playing around now with Sharky and some of the real Dixieland boys, so it'll bring back Jack to the field that he belongs in. Anything else, Bill?
